entries.english:
Know, child unborn, that this was once the greatest kingdom in all Valheim. Here lived the Sons and Daughters of the King of the Emerald Flame. Beneath his wing, we knew strength and security. In his sight, we grew like green shoots.

Now we set this stone among rubble and turn our backs on the land of our birth. May future ages take warning from us.
entries.irish:
Know, leanbh unborn, go raibh sé seo uair amháin an ríocht is mó i ngach Valheim. Seo cónaí ar an Sons agus Iníonacha an Rí an Flame Emerald. Beneath a sciathán, bhí a fhios againn neart agus slándáil. Ina radharc, d'fhás muid cosúil le bróga glasa.

Anois, leag muid an chloch seo i measc Rúbal agus cas ár ndroim ar an talamh ar ár mbreith. Bealtaine a ghlacadh aois amach anseo rabhadh uainn.

entries.english:
In the forests of the far North, our scouts came across a sleeping boy, sitting naked in the deep snow with his back to a tree. They wrapped him in furs and brought him back to the king, asleep all the while with only his eyelids moving.

We named him the Winter Child and we took him to be a good omen. May the gods have mercy on fools.
entries.irish:
I bhforaoisí an Tuaiscirt i bhfad, tháinig ár scouts ar fud buachaill codlata, ina suí naked sa sneachta domhain lena ais go dtí crann. fillte siad air i fionnaidh agus thug sé ar ais go dtí an rí, ina chodladh go léir an fad le ach a chuid eyelids ag gluaiseacht.

D'ainmnigh muid é an Linbh Gheimhridh agus thóg muid air a bheith ina omen maith. Go raibh na déithe trócaire ar fools.

entries.english:
It was known throughout the land that the two would often sit together as if in talk, the king coiled about the sleeping child with his face close, straining to catch any murmured words.

Nobody knew what passed between them but all saw the change in the king. Justice flared into wrath and caution deepened into fear. Laws were passed that must be broken and each time the lawbreakers were punished more harshly.

Tyranny came in a spiral, like a great storm.
entries.irish:
Bhí sé ar eolas ar fud an talamh go mbeadh an dá suí go minic le chéile amhail is dá mba i labhairt, coiled an rí mar gheall ar an leanbh codlata lena aghaidh gar, straining a ghabháil ar aon focail murmured.

Ní raibh a fhios ag aon duine cad a rith eatarthu ach chonaic gach an t-athrú ar an rí. Breitheamh flared isteach wrath agus rabhadh dhoimhniú i eagla. Ritheadh Dlíthe nach mór a bhriseadh agus gach uair a bhí an lawbreakers phionósú níos harshly.

Tháinig Tyranny i bíseach, cosúil le stoirm mhór.

entries.english:
When the King of the Emerald Flame flew away to visit the wizard king of the Fulings, his own thegns rose against him and torched the palace with the Winter Child inside. All of us who were alive at that time heard the shriek that sounded for the nine days of the fire and echoed in the city's streets for many weeks longer.

Those were the last good days any of us knew, before the return of our king.
entries.irish:
Nuair a theith an Rí an Flame Emerald ar shiúl chun cuairt a thabhairt ar an rí draoi na Fulings, d'ardaigh a thegns féin ina choinne agus torched an Pálás leis an Linbh Gheimhridh taobh istigh. Gach duine againn a bhí beo ag an am sin chuala an shriek a sounded do na naoi lá an tine agus macalla i sráideanna na cathrach ar feadh go leor seachtainí níos faide.

Ba iad sin na laethanta maith deiridh aon cheann de dúinn a fhios, roimh an tuairisceán ar ár rí.

entries.english:
When the king saw the charred remains of his great hall, he swore to show his foes a fire far greater than the little spark they had kindled. With his breath, he razed our city to the ground and then brought war to all the land. Some of the people stayed faithful to the king but many sought to quench his fury.

Brothers fought against brothers, sisters against sisters. The Kingdom of the Emerald Flame tore itself apart. Now only these charred ruins remain, within which not even the dead can find rest.
entries.irish:
Nuair a chonaic an rí na hiarsmaí charred a halla mór, mhionnaigh sé a thaispeáint a foes tine i bhfad níos mó ná an spréach beag a bhí fhadaigh siad. Leis an anáil, razed sé ár gcathair ar an talamh agus ansin thug cogadh ar an talamh. D'fhan cuid de na daoine dílis don rí ach d'iarr go leor a quench a Fury.

Throid Bráithre i gcoinne deartháireacha, deirfiúracha i gcoinne deirfiúracha. Ríocht an Flame Emerald tore féin ar leith. Anois ach na fothracha charred fós, nach féidir fiú na marbh teacht ar chuid eile.

entries.english: The stones tell of a great tragedy in this land, many centuries ago. It is hard to believe the creature who stalks this ruined city was once a noble beast and a wise king. Yet we will not stay our hands on this account. When we kill him, we will count it a mercy.
entries.irish: Na clocha insint tragóid mór sa talamh, go leor céadta bliain ó shin. Tá sé deacair a chreidiúint go raibh an creature a gais an chathair scriosta uair amháin Beast uasal agus rí ciallmhar. Ach ní bheidh muid ag fanacht ár lámha ar an gcuntas seo. Nuair a mharú againn dó, beidh muid ag comhaireamh sé trócaire.

entries.english: I have not been happy for more than a day in any place since I came here but this place is the worst of all. Most things are on fire and the fishing is not good. These are the words of Ulf.
entries.irish: Ní raibh mé sásta ar feadh níos mó ná lá in aon áit ó tháinig mé anseo ach is é an áit seo an ceann is measa ar fad. Tá an chuid is mó rudaí ar dóiteáin agus nach bhfuil an iascaireacht go maith. Is iad seo na focail de Ulf.

entries.english:
The pure fire of a grand drake has the power to give life and quicken the dead earth. Once, they blessed the land and seas with their cleansing flame, bringing new life wherever they passed.

But for those who are burned by a drake's fire, the blessing is a curse. They are killed and quickened at the same time, caught forever between death and life. Such are the unfortunate souls who wander this ruined land, with flames for flesh and agony in every moment. They cannot be destroyed, only pitied.
entries.irish:
Tá an tine íon de drake mhór an chumhacht a thabhairt saol agus quicken an domhain marbh. Chomh luath agus, bheannaigh siad an talamh agus farraigí lena lasair cleansing, a thabhairt saol nua cibé áit a rith siad.

Ach dóibh siúd atá dóite ag tine drake, is é an bheannacht a curse. Tá siad maraíodh agus quickened ag an am céanna, gafa go deo idir bás agus an saol. Is iad sin an anamacha trua a wander an talamh scriosta, le lasracha le haghaidh flesh agus agony i ngach nóiméad. Ní féidir iad a scriosadh, ach pitied.

entries.english:
If the tales are true, the gods long ago abandoned this world. The King of the Emerald Flame was the closest to a god we knew but our prayers to him have turned to ashes in our mouths.

This is the last of our strongholds and in the morning we will die defending it. We offer no more prayers and wish only for clean, free deaths, unburned by the flame.
entries.irish:
Má tá na scéalta fíor, tréigthe na déithe fada ó shin an domhan seo. Ba é an Rí an Flame Emerald an gaire do dia a fhios againn ach ár paidreacha dó iompú le luaithreach in ár mbéal.

Is é seo an ceann deireanach dár láidreachtaí agus ar maidin beidh muid bás a chosaint. Cuirimid aon paidreacha níos mó agus is mian ach amháin le haghaidh glan, básanna saor in aisce, unburned ag an lasair.

entries.english:
It is folly for the free folk to say they need no gods. Nobody needs gods and the gods need no one. They owe nothing to men.

But still the wise will seek the powerful as vines will seek a mighty tree to climb. We give our swords to the King of the Emerald Flame because without him there is only death.
entries.irish:
Tá sé folly do na tíre saor in aisce a rá nach gá iad aon déithe. Ní mór aon duine déithe agus na déithe aon duine. Níl siad aon rud le fir.

Ach fós beidh an ciallmhar a lorg an cumhachtach mar fíniúnacha a lorg crann mighty a dhreapadh. Tugaimid ár claimhte don Rí an Flame Emerald mar gheall ar gan dó nach bhfuil ach bás.

entries.english:
War is a fire
And men are fuel.

When the heart-blaze kindles
Their bodies are dry wood.
entries.irish:
Is cogadh dóiteáin
Agus tá fir breosla.

Nuair a bhíonn an croí-blaze kindles
Tá a gcuid comhlachtaí adhmad tirim.

entries.english: I am Astrid of the Long Arm. I came here after much hardship to fight the beast and break the curse that keeps me here. The raven has returned a memory to me and it will not let me rest. I will die as many times as I need to die to see my son again.
entries.irish: Tá mé Astrid an Arm Fada. Tháinig mé anseo tar éis cruatan i bhfad chun troid an Beast agus briseadh an curse go gcoinníonn dom anseo. Tá an raven ar ais cuimhne dom agus ní bheidh sé in iúl dom chuid eile. Beidh mé bás oiread agus is gá dom a bás a fheiceáil mo mhac arís.

entries.english: I have watched many warriors throw themselves against the beast again and again, losing a little of their will each time until their beds lie empty. If this is my fate, so be it. These are the words of Björn, who was once a farmer.
entries.irish: Tá mé ag faire go leor laochra caith iad féin i gcoinne an Beast arís agus arís, a chailliúint beagán de a n-uacht gach uair go dtí go mbeidh a gcuid leapacha folamh. Más é seo mo cinniúint, mar sin é. Is iad seo na focail Björn, a bhí uair amháin feirmeoir.

entries.english: Beware the deep trees, beware the true dark. When the night comes, keep close to your fire.
entries.irish: Beware na crainn domhain, beware an dorcha fíor. Nuair a thagann an oíche, a choinneáil gar do do dóiteáin.

entries.english: Beneath the ground, the roots of the forest twine together on a great loom. Pluck one thread and the whole weave will move. Chop down one tree and all the wood will know. Make yourself known to the One Who Walks, and he will seek you out.
entries.irish: Beneath an talamh, fréamhacha na foraoise le chéile ar loom mór. Pluck snáithe amháin agus beidh an weave ar fad bogadh. Chop síos crann amháin agus beidh a fhios ag an adhmad go léir. Déan tú féin ar eolas ag an One Who Walks, agus beidh sé ag lorg tú amach.

entries.english: I was Harald, a man from the coast. I remember nothing more of my life in Midgard except that I was a warrior. In my dreams I see the faces of those I killed. I leave this stone that at least my name will remain.
entries.irish: Bhí mé Harald, fear ón gcósta. Is cuimhin liom rud ar bith níos mó de mo shaol i Midgard ach amháin go raibh mé ina laoch. I mo bhrionglóidí feicim aghaidheanna na ndaoine a mharaigh mé. Fágann mé an chloch seo go bhfanfaidh mo ainm ar a laghad.

entries.english: Rest awhile and remember Ulf, who carved this stone with his own hand but could think of nothing to say.
entries.irish: Rest awhile agus cuimhnigh Ulf, a snoite an chloch lena lámh féin ach d'fhéadfadh smaoineamh ar rud ar bith a rá.

entries.english: Beware the Old One. The ravens say that in ages past he was a shoot of great Yggdrasil itself and a force of wisdom in the days when men and trees were friends. Now he scorns the axe and sets himself against the works of the Gods themselves. Oden banished him here for his pride but his roots are deep.
entries.irish: Beware an ceann Sean. Deir na ravens go raibh sé ina shoot de Yggdrasil mór féin agus fórsa eagna sna laethanta nuair a bhí fir agus crainn cairde. Anois scorns sé an axe agus leagann sé féin i gcoinne na n-oibreacha na Gods féin. Oden banished dó anseo as a bród ach tá a chuid fréamhacha domhain.

entries.english: We who were carried here by the Valkyrie are not the first men in this land. I have seen with my own eyes the halls they made beneath the ground and the ruins of their towers. Will the same fate await us?
entries.irish: Níl muid a rinne anseo ag an Valkyrie na chéad fir sa talamh seo. Feicthe agam le mo shúile féin na hallaí a rinne siad faoi bhun na talún agus na fothracha a gcuid túir. An mbeidh an chinniúint chéanna ag fanacht linn?

entries.english: Eight were the creatures banished to this world by mighty Oden in the first days of his kingship. Eight Gods and monsters too proud to bear his yoke. I have heard the tread of the Old Ones in the forest and have crouched in the shadow of the Mountain Mother when she flies. Of the others I know little. I will add to this stone when I have seen more.
entries.irish: Ocht bhí na créatúir banished leis an domhan ag mighty Oden sa chéad lá dá ríthe. Ocht Gods agus arrachtaigh ró-bhródúil a iompróidh a cuing. Chuala mé an tread na cinn Sean san fhoraois agus tá crouched i scáth an Mháthair Sléibhe nuair a cuileoga sí. As na daoine eile a fhios agam beag. Cuirfidh mé leis an gcloch seo nuair a chonaic mé níos mó.

entries.english:
The trolls of Midgard may be fading from your memory, as indeed they are from all the race of man. Few and forlorn, they crouch in damp caves and gnaw on the bones of the weak and foolhardy. The will of Oden has pushed them back into the dark places.

But in Valheim they have flourished. It has been centuries since any in Midgard saw the great trolls stamp flat the land and bring down the trees for joy. Look upon this great and noble sight, wanderers in a strange land! Then take to your heels and run...
entries.irish:
Is féidir leis an trolls de Midgard a céimnithe ó do chuimhne, mar go deimhin, tá siad ó gach cine an duine. Few agus forlorn, crouch siad i uaimheanna taise agus gnaw ar na cnámha an lag agus foolhardy. Tá toil Oden bhrúigh iad ar ais isteach sna háiteanna dorcha.

Ach i Valheim tá siad rath. Tá sé na céadta bliain ó aon i Midgard chonaic an stampa trolls mór cothrom an talamh agus a thabhairt síos na crainn le haghaidh áthas. Féach ar an radharc iontach agus uasal, wanderers i dtalamh aisteach! Ansin a chur ar do sála agus a reáchtáil...

entries.english: Raised by the Old Man of the Forest from seeds of sin, the greydwarfs clothe themselves in the human forms they once knew, but there is no longer any warmth in their hearts. They live now only to serve the Elder and to protect the wood. Do not let pity for them stay your hand.
entries.irish: Raised ag an Man Sean na Foraoise ó shíolta de sin, an greydwarfs clothe iad féin i bhfoirmeacha an duine a fhios acu uair amháin, ach níl a thuilleadh aon teas ina gcroí. Tá cónaí orthu anois ach chun freastal ar an Elder agus an t-adhmad a chosaint. Ná lig trua dóibh fanacht ar do lámh.

entries.english:
Which among you was a murderer, a kin-slayer, a renegade? Who turned a blade in their brother's back? Who tore babes from their mothers' arms, set fire to the houses of the plundered? Consider it a blessing that you remember nothing. Each among you is a great warrior, and warriors' souls are never clean.

But Oden has gifted you a second chance... Praise the Allfather!
entries.irish:
Cén measc a bhí tú murderer, a kin-slayer, a renegade? Cé a iompaigh lann ina deartháir ar ais? Cé a babes Strac as a n-arm máithreacha ', tine a leagtar ar na tithe an argain? Smaoinigh air a blessing go cuimhin leat rud ar bith. Tá gach i measc tú laoch mór, agus laochra' anamacha riamh glan.

Ach tá Oden cumasach tú dara seans... Moladh an Allfather!

entries.english: Look to the sky where mighty Yggdrasil reaches out, called by the Forsaken Ones to join itself once more with this wayward world. It is a glorious sight but a dreadful one. For as the great tree bends out across the void, its branches strain and crack, felt in the remaining nine worlds as quakings of the earth, great storms and holy fires. The Forsaken must be slain and balance restored.
entries.irish: Féach ar an spéir nuair a shroicheann mighty Yggdrasil amach, ar a dtugtar na cinn Forsaken a bheith páirteach féin uair amháin níos mó leis an domhan wayward. Is radharc glórmhar é ach ceann uafásach. I gcás mar bends an crann mór amach ar fud an neamhní, a brainsí brú agus crack, bhraith sna naoi saol atá fágtha mar quakings an domhain, stoirmeacha mór agus tinte naofa. Ní mór na Forsaken a slain agus cothromaíocht ar ais.

entries.english: Astrid will not look at me twice. I leave this stone to honour great Freya. O goddess, grant me a beard like Bjorn's that I might win her heart!
entries.irish: Ní bheidh Astrid breathnú ar dom faoi dhó. Fágann mé an chloch seo chun ómós mór Freya. O bandia, dheonú dom féasóg cosúil Bjorn go mb'fhéidir go mbeadh mé a bhuachan a croí!

entries.english:
I have been reborn many times in this world. I have died again and again only to awaken in my own house. Yet still I wonder how many more times I will return like this. Frida was taken by a serpent and her bed lies empty still. Bjarni was bitten in half by a troll and neither half has been seen since...

All around are the ruins of those who came before us but where are the hands that built them?

Perhaps, when a warrior loses the will to remain here, they can no longer return...
entries.irish:
Bhí mé reborn uair go leor sa domhan seo. Mé a fuair bás arís agus arís ach a mhúscailt i mo theach féin. Ach fós Wonder mé cé mhéad uair níos mó beidh mé ar ais mar seo. Tógadh Frida ag nathair agus tá a leaba folamh fós. Bhí bitten Bjarni i leath ag troll agus nach bhfuil leath le feiceáil ó...

Tá gach timpeall na fothracha na ndaoine a tháinig os ár gcomhair ach nuair a bhfuil na lámha a thóg iad?

B'fhéidir, nuair a chailleann laoch an uacht chun fanacht anseo, is féidir leo a thuilleadh ar ais...

entries.english: COOK THEIR REMAINS
entries.irish: COOK ATHBHREITHNITHE

entries.english:
The depths of the cave promised me riches.
Down turns out, is easier than up.
The lake helped best it could, but it could only do so much.
It took me strength to not empty it completely, to leave you weary traveler a chance just as I had.
I hope you came here more prepared than I.
If not, there is room here next to me, to just lay down and.. rest.
entries.irish:
An doimhneacht an uaimh gealladh riches dom.
Casadh an Dúin amach, tá sé níos éasca ná suas.
Chuidigh an loch is fearr d'fhéadfadh sé, ach d'fhéadfadh sé a dhéanamh ach an oiread sin.
Thóg sé neart dom gan folamh sé go hiomlán, a fhágáil tú taistealaí traochta deis díreach mar a bhí mé.
Tá súil agam gur tháinig tú anseo níos ullmhaithe ná mé.
Más rud é nach, tá seomra anseo in aice liom, a leagan díreach síos agus.. chuid eile.

entries.english:
This cliff I climbed in in hopes of reaching the top.
Regretfully the cave was too deep.
...
Back here again considering the jump.
Alas, the coward I am is climbing back down.
entries.irish:
An aill climbed mé i súil a bhaint amach an barr.
Regretfully bhí an uaimh ró-domhain.
...
Ar ais anseo arís ag smaoineamh ar an léim.
Faraoir, an coward Tá mé ag dreapadh ar ais síos.

entries.english: Ancient Cave Markings
entries.irish: Cave Ársa Marcáil

entries.english:
The Deep North. The final obstacle before I can prove myself worthy.

The trials have been many, and so have the deaths. I have lost friends dear to me.

But at last I am here.
entries.irish:
An Domhain Thuaidh. An constaic deiridh sular féidir liom a chruthú fiú féin.

Bhí na trialacha go leor, agus mar sin tá na básanna. Tá mé caillte cairde daor dom.

Ach ar deireadh tá mé anseo.

entries.english:
It seems peaceful enough. So far, the wildlife doesn’t appear to care much for my presence here.

I should be able to gather some valuable resources from them if I need to. It’s my survival or theirs, after all.
entries.irish:
Dealraíonn sé síochánta go leor. Go dtí seo, nach bhfuil an fiadhúlra le feiceáil chun aire a thabhairt i bhfad do mo láthair anseo.

Ba chóir dom a bheith in ann a bhailiú roinnt acmhainní luachmhar uathu más gá dom a. Tá sé mo mharthanas nó inniúlacht siúd, tar éis an tsaoil.

entries.english:
I have to be on my guard. Few places have been peaceful since I first arrived here, and it would be foolish to believe these lands to be different.

No matter how well I fight, I might still be overcome by the inevitable cold of the place.

I’d best find some shelter.
entries.irish:
Caithfidh mé a bheith ar mo garda. Roinnt áiteanna a bheith síochánta ó tháinig mé ar dtús anseo, agus bheadh sé foolish chun a chreidiúint na tailte a bheith difriúil.

Is cuma cé chomh maith agus mé ag troid, D'fhéadfadh mé a bheith fós a shárú ag an fuar dosheachanta na háite.

Ba mhaith liom a fháil is fearr roinnt foscadh.

entries.english: So far I’ve been left alone. Despite that, I can’t shake the feeling that something is watching me.
entries.irish: Go dtí seo tá mé fágtha ina n-aonar. In ainneoin sin, ní féidir liom a chroitheadh an mothú go bhfuil rud éigin ag breathnú orm.

entries.english: I found an old building, but it was deserted. It’s hard to say for how long, but I don’t believe I’ll find any friends here.
entries.irish: Fuair mé foirgneamh d'aois, ach bhí sé tréigthe. Tá sé deacair a rá cé chomh fada, ach ní chreidim go mbainfidh mé teacht ar aon chairde anseo.

entries.english:
I don’t like to think about what could have happened, had my axe not been as sharp nor my senses as keen. After all, there is no one left to come to my aid.

I may have lost my companions. But it is for their sake that I must continue. The ruler of these lands must die.
entries.irish:
Ní maith liom smaoineamh ar cad a d'fhéadfadh a tharla, bhí mo axe nach raibh chomh géar ná mo céadfaí mar fonn. Tar éis an tsaoil, níl aon duine fágtha chun teacht ar mo chabhair.

Is féidir liom a bheith caillte mo companions. Ach tá sé ar a son nach mór dom leanúint ar aghaidh. Ní mór do rialtóir na dtailte bás.

entries.english:
It’s strange. I can’t help but feel like there should be people here, just waiting to welcome me.

I think the winters looked like this when I was a child, and any moment my father should be welcoming me home. But he isn’t here. No one is.
entries.irish:
Tá sé aisteach. Ní féidir liom cabhrú ach dar mhaith ba chóir go mbeadh daoine anseo, ach ag fanacht chun fáilte a chur roimh dom.

I mo thuairimse, d'fhéach an gheimhridh mar seo nuair a bhí mé leanbh, agus ba chóir aon nóiméad mo athair a bheith fáilteach dom abhaile. Ach nach bhfuil sé anseo. Níl aon duine.

entries.english:
I have been haunted by dreams lately, in which I am a raven. On great, black wings I soar across this world that I’ve come to know, but it is not the same.

The landscape has gone from green and fertile to cold and barren. Perhaps it is just this frozen north that has been getting to me. Yet...what if it’s not?
entries.irish:
Bhí mé haunted ag aisling go déanach, ina bhfuil mé raven. Ar mór, sciatháin dubh soar mé ar fud an domhain go bhfuil mé ag teacht ar an eolas, ach nach bhfuil sé mar an gcéanna.

Tá an tírdhreach imithe ó glas agus torthúil go fuar agus barren. B'fhéidir go bhfuil sé ach an ó thuaidh reoite go bhfuil ag fáil dom. Ach... cad mura bhfuil sé?

entries.english:
I know now where I need to go. The Ancestors have pointed me in the direction of the one who rules these lands, the one they tried to keep in chains but whose power now shackles the very world.

If I can just slay this foe, this hateful being, I will have proven myself once and for all.
entries.irish:
Tá a fhios agam anois nuair is gá dom dul. Tá an Ancestors fios dom i dtreo an duine a rialacha na tailte, an ceann a rinne siad a choinneáil i slabhraí ach a bhfuil cumhacht geimhle anois ar an domhan an-.

Más féidir liom a slay ach an foe, seo a bheith hateful, beidh mé ag cruthaithe mé féin uair amháin agus do gach.

entries.english:
The mighty ones who came before us rest here.
Tread warily, as their slumber may yet be disturbed.
entries.irish:
Na cinn mighty a tháinig roimh dúinn chuid eile anseo.
Tread warily, mar is féidir a gcuid slumber a chur isteach go fóill.

entries.english:
Death comes for all, in the end, even the mightiest of warriors.
One day you may be counted amongst them.
entries.irish:
Bás thagann do gach, sa deireadh, fiú an mightiest de laochra.
Lá amháin is féidir leat a chomhaireamh ina measc.

entries.english:
Let us honour our ancestors, who carved this world that we now live in.
And may they deem us worthy.
entries.irish:
Lig dúinn onóir ár sinsear, a snoite an domhan go bhfuil cónaí orainn anois i.
Agus féadfaidh siad a mheas dúinn fiú.

entries.english: Ancestral Memorial
entries.irish: Seirbhís do Chustaiméirí

entries.english: Lore: Ancestral Memorial
entries.irish: Lore: Cuimhneachán ancestral

entries.english: At first this seemed a good home for Ulf, who liked the cold and the snow. Then came the mean little creatures, intent on dragging me below, and I was forced to reconsider.
entries.irish: Ar dtús bhí an chuma seo ina bhaile maith do Ulf, a thaitin leis an fuar agus an sneachta. Ansin tháinig na créatúir meán beag, hintinn ar dragging mé thíos, agus bhí iachall orm a athbhreithniú.

entries.english:
If what the raven says is true, there is only one more forsaken I must slay. But what comes after? Will my son truly be returned to me, or I to him?

Astrid raised this stone for her son, should he follow in her footsteps before she gets to see him again.
entries.irish:
Má tá an méid a deir an raven fíor, níl ach forsaken amháin níos mó ní mór dom a slay. Ach cad a thagann tar éis? An mbeidh mo mhac a chur ar ais go fírinneach dom, nó mé dó?

Astrid ardaigh an chloch as a mac, ba chóir dó a leanúint ina footsteps sula bhfaigheann sí a fheiceáil dó arís.

entries.english: These lands seemed so familiar, awakening memories buried deep within our minds. We should have known they were not all that they seemed.
entries.irish: Dhealraigh na tailte sin chomh eolach, awakening cuimhní curtha domhain laistigh dár n-intinn. Ba chóir dúinn a bheith ar eolas nach raibh siad go léir gur chuma siad.

entries.english: Heed the words of Kata, who once thought the trolls of the forest were mighty foes. Their kin in these lands are tall as the tallest of towers, and harder than the hardest of stones, but those who manage to slay them stand to reap a glimmering reward.
entries.irish: Heed na focail de Kata, a shíl uair amháin go raibh na trolls na foraoise foes mighty. Tá a n-craiceann sna tailte ard mar an airde de túir, agus níos deacra ná an deacra de clocha, ach iad siúd a bhainistiú a slay iad seasamh a bhaint luach saothair glimmering.

entries.english:
When we first arrived here, this place was rich and prosperous. But the winters are colder and longer now, and we fear they might soon take over altogether.

Yet, here we have built our homes and here we have grown our roots, so here it is that we shall stay.
entries.irish:
Nuair a tháinig muid ar dtús anseo, bhí an áit seo saibhir agus rathúil. Ach tá na geimhreadh níos fuaire agus níos faide anois, agus eagla orainn d'fhéadfadh siad a ghlacadh go luath ar láimh ar fad.

Ach, anseo tá muid tógtha ár dtithe agus anseo tá muid tar éis fás ár fréamhacha, mar sin anseo tá sé go mbeidh muid ag fanacht.

entries.english:
In the farthest north
Where magic dances in the skies
Offer to call forth
What just below the surface lies

Let the coals burn bright
Ancestral wisdom waits for those
Who should stand to fight
Their elders' mighty blades and bows
entries.irish:
Sa faide ó thuaidh
Sa chás go damhsaí draíochta sna sciálaithe
Tairiscint chun glaoch amach
Cad díreach faoi bhun an dromchla luíonn

Lig an gual sruthán geal
Fanann eagna Ancestral dóibh siúd
Cé ba chóir seasamh chun troid
A elders ' lanna mighty agus bows

entries.english: Beware of false trees! Chiming icicles and creaking branches might not just be moving in the wind...
entries.irish: Beware crainn bréagach! Ní fhéadfadh icicles chiming agus brainsí creaking a bheith ag gluaiseacht ach sa ghaoth...

entries.english: Signe raised this stone in memory of Eigil, who fell in battle. He had yet to learn that not everything here is as frozen as it first seems.
entries.irish: D'ardaigh Comharthaí an chloch seo i gcuimhne ar Eigil, a thit i cath. Bhí sé fós a fhoghlaim nach bhfuil gach rud anseo mar reoite mar is cosúil sé ar dtús.

entries.english:
Buried beneath the snow, deep within the north,
bonds harden like frozen earth
as truth begins to thaw.
entries.irish:
Buried faoi bhun an sneachta, domhain laistigh de thuaidh,
bannaí cruaite cosúil le talamh reoite
mar a thosaíonn fírinne a thaw.

entries.english: SACRIFICE HER SPAWN
entries.irish: SACRIFICE ANSEO

entries.english:
Let you who read me be aware of the Frost wyrms, one of the most ancient kins sprung from Ymir's body.

The most common form of the wyrm are the Drakes, the small males who care for the offspring. Most often they can be seen poised by rocky nests guarding the eggs. In contrast, the females are much larger and a rare sight to behold, but once angered they provide a vicious foe.
entries.irish:
Lig duit a léamh dom a bheith ar an eolas faoi na wyrms Frost, ar cheann de na braithí is ársa sprung ó chomhlacht Ymir ar.

Is iad an fhoirm is coitianta den wyrm na Drakes, na fir beaga a thugann aire don sliocht. Is minic is féidir iad a fheiceáil poised ag neadacha creagach ag cosaint na n-uibheacha. I gcodarsnacht leis sin, tá na mná i bhfad níos mó agus radharc annamh a behold, ach nuair a angered siad a chur ar fáil foe fí.

entries.english: Lore: Drake
entries.irish: Lore: Drake

entries.english:
Long ages ago, the world of Valheim was home to a race of proud and noble people. They built great towers which touched the clouds and delved deep into the earth for precious metals. But their pride was their undoing. They challenged the very Gods and went to war against the Aesir and the Vanir, destroying themselves completely. Great Oden levelled their cities and Loki consumed their mines in fire. Mighty Thor broke down their towers and Freya sowed their fields with salt tears.

Now they are sunk many hundreds of years deep. No songs sing of their stories, and the earth has claimed their cities. But pride cannot be killed entirely and the warriors who fought in that final battle will not surrender until their bodies are dust and the dust long gone. They return as Draugr, unholy walkers in ancient armour, creatures of rust and despair.

Break them, bury them, let them know they are dead.
entries.irish:
A aois fada ó shin, bhí an domhan de Valheim baile le cine de dhaoine bródúil agus uasal. Thóg siad túir mhór a dteagmháil léi na scamaill agus delved domhain isteach sa domhan le haghaidh miotail lómhara. Ach bhí a n-bród a gan déanamh. Dhúshlán siad na Dia an-agus chuaigh siad chun cogaidh i gcoinne an Aesir agus an Vanir, scriosadh iad féin go hiomlán. Great Oden levelled a gcuid cathracha agus Loki ól a mianaigh i tine. minicíocht uisce: flúirseach Thor bhris síos a gcuid túir agus Freya chuir a réimsí le deora salann.

Anois tá siad sunk na céadta bliain go leor domhain. Níl aon amhrán chanadh a gcuid scéalta, agus tá an domhain éiligh a gcuid cathracha. Ach ní féidir bród a maraíodh go hiomlán agus ní bheidh na laochra a throid sa cath deiridh thabhairt suas go dtí go bhfuil a n-chomhlachtaí deannaigh agus an deannaigh imithe i bhfad. Fill siad mar Draugr, siúlóidí unholy i armúr ársa, créatúir de meirge agus éadóchas.

Briseadh iad, iad a adhlacadh, lig dóibh a fhios go bhfuil siad marbh.

entries.english: Take care, warrior. You've happened upon an outpost of the forlorn Dvergr clans, long since separated from their kin in Nidavellir. Trapped here they still toil, expecting reprieve that will never come. It is a sad fate...
entries.irish: Tabhair aire, laoch. Tá tú a tharla ar outpost na clans Forlorn Dvergr, fada ó scartha óna n-kin i Nidavellir. Trapped anseo toil siad fós, ag súil reprieve a bheidh riamh teacht. Is saill brónach é...

entries.english: Munin: Dvergr homes
entries.irish: Mumhan: Tithe Dvergr

entries.english:
These are the Dvergrhomes, built long ago in a gilded age... Their splendour rivalled the Golden Hall itself!

Regrettably, nothing can last forever. The halls below and the treasures left within are now guarded by more sinister lodgers.
entries.irish:
Is iad seo na Dvergrhomes, a tógadh i bhfad ó shin i aois gilded... A splendour rivalled an Halla Órga féin!

Regrettably, is féidir aon rud deireanach go deo. Tá na hallaí thíos agus na seoda taobh istigh cosanta anois ag níos mó taisceoirí sinister.

entries.english: Shadows of an ancient age. The Jotunn once ruled the tenth world, until their time ran out and they were ousted by some other power.
entries.irish: Scáthanna d'aois ársa. An Jotunn Rialaigh uair amháin ar an domhan deichiú, go dtí go rith a gcuid ama amach agus bhí siad ousted ag roinnt cumhachta eile.

entries.english: AND HIS DYING SOUL WAS SPLIT AND SHARED AMONG ALL HIS KIN

entries.english:
Let all who read me beware of the Greydwarfs, the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones. They are born from rot and rainfall, they spring like mushrooms from the smoking soil. There is nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes, those who fear nothing should still fear them.

When the soul of a murderer or a great sinner rots under the ground, it makes a hollow cyst which draws rock and wood and moss to it. It gathers up the peat into flesh, braids reeds into bone and takes rags for skin.

It should not walk but when the night comes it walks. Should you who read this see one with a sword to your hand, lance it and let it out. Or put it to the torch, for it fears the flame.
entries.irish:
Lig gach a léamh beware dom an Greydwarfs, na skulkers sa dorchadas, na cinn soulless. Rugadh iad ó lobhadh agus báisteach, is maith leo beacáin ón ithir tobac. Níl aon rud ar a gcuid teangacha nó taobh thiar a súile, iad siúd a eagla ba chóir aon rud eagla fós iad.

Nuair a bheidh anam de murderer nó rots peacach mór faoin talamh, a dhéanann sé cistéin log a tharraingíonn carraig agus adhmad agus caonach dó. Bailíonn sé suas an móin i flesh, déanann braids ithe isteach i gcnámh agus tógann sé ceirteacha le haghaidh craicinn.

Níor chóir dó siúl ach nuair a thagann an oíche siúlóidí. Ar chóir duit a léamh seo a fheiceáil ar cheann le claíomh ar do lámh, lance sé agus lig sé amach. Nó é a chur chuig an torch, le haghaidh eagla sé an lasair.

entries.english: Lore: Greydwarfs

entries.english:
Long ago, the Allfather Oden united the worlds. He threw down his foes and cast them into the tenth world, then split the boughs which held their prison to the World-Tree, and left it to drift unanchored, a place of exile…



For centuries, this world slumbered uneasily. But it did not die... As glacial ages passed, kingdoms rose and fell out of sight of the Gods.



When Oden heard his enemies were growing once again in strength, he looked to Midgard and sent his Valkyries to scour the battlefields for the greatest of their warriors. Dead to the world, they would be born again…



…in VALHEIM!
entries.irish:
Fada ó shin, d'aontaigh an Allfather Oden na saol. Chaith sé síos a chuid foes agus chaith siad isteach sa domhan deichiú, scoilt ansin na boughs a bhí ina bpríosún go dtí an Domhan-Tree, agus d'fhág sé a sruth unanchored, áit deor...



Ar feadh na gcéadta bliain, slumbered an domhan uneasily. Ach ní raibh sé bás... Mar aois oighearshruth rith, d'ardaigh ríochtaí agus thit amach as radharc na Dia.



Nuair a chuala Oden a naimhde a bhí ag fás arís i neart, d'fhéach sé go Midgard agus chuir sé a chuid Valkyries a scour na catha don chuid is mó dá laochra. Marbh ar fud an domhain, bheadh siad a rugadh arís...



... i VALHEIM!

entries.english: To prove you are worthy of entering Valhalla you have been sent to Valheim, the tenth Norse world. Only by defeating the mighty beasts of these lands will you win the favor of the Gods.
entries.irish: A chruthú go bhfuil tú fiú dul isteach Valhalla bhfuil tú curtha chuig Valheim, an domhan deichiú Norse. Ach amháin trí defeating na beithigh mighty de na tailte a bheidh tú bua an bhfabhar na Dia.

entries.english:
This land is hard and wild but we who are brought here are harder still. Take comfort, traveller, in the gifts before you, the good wood and stone, the fruits and flowers of the forest.

Look also to the wild boar who roam these lands. They fear fire and the hand of man but they can be taught to obey it. Go quietly to them and let them eat of your stock. Roots of the ground are their pleasure.
entries.irish:
Tá an talamh crua agus fiáin ach táimid a thabhairt anseo níos deacra fós. Tóg compord, taistealaí, sna bronntanais roimh tú, an adhmad maith agus cloch, torthaí agus bláthanna na foraoise.

Féach freisin ar an boar fiáin a roam na tailte. eagla siad tine agus an lámh an duine ach is féidir iad a mhúineadh a obey sé. Téigh go ciúin leo agus lig dóibh a ithe de do stoc. Is iad na fréamhacha na talún a pléisiúir.

entries.english: Lore: Boars
entries.irish: irl - Library Service

entries.english:
Where the grass grows underfoot

And the sky is blue overhead

There will always be a hearth and a home
entries.irish:
Nuair a fhásann an féar underfoot

Agus is é an spéir lasnairde gorm

Beidh a bheith i gcónaí hearth agus baile

entries.english:
Long ages past, when the Allfather Oden united the worlds, he threw down the Vanir, the giants and those creatures older than any others. The greatest of them could not be killed but were instead Forsaken, exiled here to Valheim for eternity.

When they tread the earth, the lesser creatures jump like crumbs on a drumskin. You will know them when you see them.
entries.irish:
Aosaithe fada anuas, nuair a aontaithe an Allfather Oden an saol, chaith sé síos an Vanir, na giants agus na créatúir níos sine ná aon daoine eile. Ní fhéadfaí an mó acu a maraíodh ach bhí ina ionad sin Forsaken, exiled anseo chun Valheim le haghaidh eternity.

Nuair a tread siad an domhain, na créatúir níos lú léim cosúil le crumbs ar drumaskin. Beidh a fhios agat iad nuair a fheiceann tú iad.

entries.english:
Give thanks to Frey for the rain and sun

For the shoots that break the earth's skin

And the fruits of the vine

Give thanks to Oden for the flesh and bone

The smoke from the cooking fire, the warm pelt

And the strength of your arm
entries.irish:
Tabhair buíochas le Frey don bháisteach agus don ghrian

Maidir leis na bróga a bhriseann craiceann an domhain

Agus torthaí na fíniúna

Tabhair buíochas le Oden as an flesh agus cnámh

An deataigh ón tine cócaireachta, an pelt te

Agus an neart do lámh

entries.english: Hold, traveller, and bear witness to my warning. We are many who have come before you, carried here by Oden's will to do his work. The path ahead is hard and the dangers great. If you hold your life dear, keep to these meadows and make your dwelling away from the trees. Fear the Horned One and the creatures he will send against you.
entries.irish: Coinnigh, taistealaí, agus iompróidh an finné ar mo rabhadh. Is iomaí duine a tháinig os a gcomhair, a rinne Oden anseo chun a chuid oibre a dhéanamh. Is é an cosán amach romhainn crua agus na contúirtí mór. Má tá tú i seilbh do daor saol, a choinneáil ar na móinéir agus a dhéanamh do theaghais ar shiúl ó na crainn. Eagla an ceann Horned agus na créatúir beidh sé a sheoladh i gcoinne tú.

entries.english:
Heed these words of Ulf, a poor settler in a strange land. You will find here good stone and wood, all you need to build a house. You will need to craft a roof to keep out the rain. Then you will need walls to stop the roof from falling down. Finally, you must have a door or it will be much harder to go in and out.

These things Ulf has learned for himself. Now he writes them on this stone to help others. Pray to Oden for his soul.
entries.irish:
Heed na focail Ulf, settler bocht i dtalamh aisteach. Gheobhaidh tú cloch agus adhmad maith anseo, is gá duit teach a thógáil. Beidh ort a ceardaíochta díon a choinneáil amach an bháisteach. Ansin beidh ort ballaí chun stop a chur leis an díon ó titim síos. Ar deireadh, ní mór duit doras nó beidh sé i bhfad níos deacra dul isteach agus amach.

Tá na rudaí Ulf fhoghlaim dó féin. Anois scríobhann sé iad ar an gcloch chun cabhrú le daoine eile. Pray go Oden as a anam.

entries.english: I was Astrid, a shieldmaiden of the forest. I know nothing of my life before I came here but my arm remembers the sword and my eyes see the course of the arrow. Now the raven guides me and I fight the great beasts in Oden's name.
entries.irish: Bhí mé Astrid, a shieldmaiden na foraoise. Tá a fhios agam aon rud de mo shaol sula tháinig mé anseo ach mo lámh cuimhin an claíomh agus mo shúile a fheiceáil ar an gcúrsa an arrow. Anois na treoracha raven dom agus mé ag troid na beithigh mór in ainm Oden.

entries.english:
Blue-eyed shufflers in muck, the neck are small lizards native to Valheim. Surly and mean-spirited, they will attack on sight and must be destroyed like vermin. They stay near water because the creatures of the land loathe and abhor them.

Yet no creature is all bad. Their tails are delicious.
entries.irish:
Suaitheadh gorm-eyed i muc, tá an muineál lizards beag ó dhúchas go Valheim. Surly agus ciallóidh-spirited, beidh siad ionsaí ar radharc agus ní mór a scrios cosúil le vermin. Fanann siad in aice le huisce mar gheall ar na créatúir an talamh loathe agus abhor iad.

Ach tá aon creature go léir dona. Tá a n-eireabaill delicious.

entries.english: Sisters and brothers of the shield-wall, lift up your hearts! You are the greatest warriors, chosen by the Allfather himself for your courage and valor. Now death has brought you to a land where you can remake yourselves in battle and toil, winning favor and honor from the Gods! Leave your memories to rot in Midgard along with your sins, the finest part of you is here!
entries.irish: Siúracha agus deartháireacha an sciath-bhalla, ardaitheoir suas do hearts! Tá tú na laochra is mó, roghnaithe ag an Allfather féin do do misneach agus valor. Anois tá bás thug tú chun talamh áit ar féidir leat a remake díbh féin i cath agus toil, a bhuaigh bhfabhar agus onóir ó na Dia! Fág do chuid cuimhní chun lobhadh i Midgard chomh maith le do bpeacaí, an chuid is fearr de tú anseo!

entries.english: On this spot a tree fell on my head and I cursed the Gods. So I leave this stone in praise of them, that they might forgive my reckless words.
entries.irish: Ar an láthair thit crann ar mo cheann agus cursed mé na Dia. Mar sin, fág mé an chloch i moladh acu, go bhféadfadh siad logh mo focail meargánta.

entries.english: Pause, traveler. You are well come to the last and most lawless of the Ten Worlds. In Valheim, the air is pure, the water deep and clear and the forests overflowing with bounty. Here is adventure, joy and glory for the taking!
entries.irish: Úsáid, lucht siúil. Tá tú ag teacht go maith leis an deireanach agus is Lawless na Deich Worlds. I Valheim, tá an t-aer íon, an t-uisce domhain agus soiléir agus na foraoisí cur thar maoil le bounty. Seo eachtraíochta, áthas agus glóir le haghaidh an cur!

entries.english:
A full belly

A full sail

The weight of a spear to your hand

And a song on your lips

Let all the mountains crumble

And the seas boil to salt

One day in the sun is a life well-lived.
entries.irish:
A bolg iomlán

A sheoladh iomlán

An meáchan a spear do lámh

Agus amhrán ar do liopaí

Lig go léir na sléibhte crumble

Agus boil na farraige chun salann

Is lá amháin sa ghrian saol dea-beo.

entries.english:
Here lie the Jotunn, most ancient of all Oden's kin and fiercest of all his adversaries. In life they were bringers of ruin but now, in death, they nurture new growth.

What is living must die, and what is dead must be born again.
entries.irish:
Seo bréag an Jotunn, an chuid is mó ársa de gach kin Oden agus fíochmhar de gach adversaries. Sa saol bhí siad a thabhairters de ruin ach anois, i bás, nurture siad fás nua.

Ní mór Cad atá ina gcónaí bás, agus ní mór an méid atá marbh a rugadh arís.

entries.english:
Where the air is thick with magic
And the earth is quick with life,
The mist breeds wonders.
entries.irish:
Cá bhfuil an t-aer tiubh le draíocht
Agus is é an domhain tapaidh leis an saol,
Wonders na pórtha mist.

entries.english: Trust nothing in the mist. I passed through here in a group of seven people but every time we stopped to count, we counted eight. We do not know who the eighth was, but by morning they were gone.
entries.irish: Iontaobhas rud ar bith sa mist. Rith mé trí anseo i ngrúpa de sheacht duine ach gach uair a stop muid a chomhaireamh, chomhaireamh muid ocht. Níl a fhios againn a bhí an t-ochtú, ach ar maidin bhí siad imithe.

entries.english:
The Dvergr are the descendants of the great smiths of old, delvers in the deep earth, seekers of hidden treasure.

Here in Valheim they mine the bones of the Jotunn and distill eitr, the stuff of magic. If left alone, they are happy with their own plans and care little for the lives of others, but when raised they will defend themselves.
entries.irish:
Is iad an Dvergr sliocht na gabha mór d'aois, delvers sa domhan domhain, lucht iarrtha taisce i bhfolach.

Anseo i Valheim siad mianach na cnámha an Jotunn agus eitéar driog, an stuif draíochta. Má d'fhág ina n-aonar, tá siad sásta lena gcuid pleananna féin agus cúram beag do shaol daoine eile, ach nuair a ardaíodh beidh siad a chosaint féin.

entries.english:
The raven showed me how to make a staff that set my beard on fire. I will meddle no more with such things.

Weary of mist and magic, Ulf carved this stone. Now I go to find a less troublesome place.
entries.irish:
Léirigh an raven dom conas foireann a shocrú mo féasóg ar dhóiteán. Beidh mé meddle níos mó le rudaí den sórt sin.

Weary de mist agus draíochta, Ulf snoite an chloch. Anois, téann mé chun áit níos lú trioblóideacha a aimsiú.

entries.english: Heed the words of Ulf and do not take the hats of the short ones from their heads. They have no sense of a jest and the only cure for insulting them is to kill them. Also, their hats do not fit common heads.
entries.irish: Heed na focail Ulf agus nach chur ar an hataí na cinn gearr as a gceann. Tá siad aon tuiscint ar jest agus is é an leigheas amháin le haghaidh insulting iad a mharú iad. Chomh maith leis sin, ní oireann a gcuid hataí cinnirí coitianta.

entries.english:
Wanderers in fog,
Where do you go?
Not knowing what you were,
Nor seeing where you go.
entries.irish:
Wanderers i ceo,
Cá dtéann tú?
Níl a fhios agam cad a bhí tú,
Ná feiceáil nuair a théann tú.

entries.english:
Watch for him in moonlight

Haunter of the night.

Soft of foot

Sharp of tooth

Slow to stalk

Quick to bite.
entries.irish:
Féach air i solas na gealaí

Haunter na hoíche.

Bog chos

Géar fiacail

taiseachas aeir: fliuch

Tapa le bite.

entries.english: Lore: Fenring
entries.irish: Iasachtaí: Fenring

entries.english: Few of us found our way to these mountains. We were twenty and now we are two. Agda is dying, a Draugr arrow lies near her heart. I will bid her farewell beside this stone and give her ashes to the wind. Then I will turn my face to the highest peak and seek out the Winged One. May Oden give me death or glory.
entries.irish: Few againn fuair ár mbealach chun na sléibhte. Bhí muid fiche agus anois tá muid dhá. Agda ag fáil bháis, luíonn arrow Draugr in aice a croí. Cuirfidh mé a slán in aice leis an gcloch seo agus tabharfaidh sí luaithreach don ghaoth. Ansin, beidh mé ag dul mo aghaidh go dtí an buaic is airde agus a lorg amach an ceann Winged. Bealtaine Oden thabhairt dom bás nó ghlóir.

entries.english: This marks the spot where the great drake was first seen by me, Ulf, in the third summer of my life in Valheim. She stopped here to leave a pile of dung holding the bones of deer, boar and the skull of a greydwarf. I will never come near this place again.
entries.irish: Seo marcanna an láthair nuair a bhí an drake mór le feiceáil ar dtús ag dom, Ulf, sa tríú samhradh de mo shaol i Valheim. Stop sí anseo a fhágáil ar carn de aoileach a bhfuil na cnámha deer, boar agus an cloigeann de graydwarf. Ní thiocfaidh mé in aice leis an áit seo arís.

entries.english: Halt and listen, traveller. On the highest peaks of Valheim, the air is thin and fragile. From here you can sometimes catch sounds from other places, the ring of battle on Midgard, the roar of a feast in Valhalla or the shriek of a Valkyrie as she crosses the space between the worlds.
entries.irish: Halt agus éisteacht, taistealaí. Ar na beanna is airde de Valheim, tá an t-aer tanaí agus leochaileach. Ó anseo is féidir leat a ghabháil uaireanta fuaimeanna ó áiteanna eile, an fáinne cath ar Midgard, an roar féasta i Valhalla nó an shriek de Valkyrie mar a thrasnaíonn sí an spás idir na saol.

entries.english: Where this stands I once saw the great drake flying above me and I hid in a bush until she passed. Ulf the Brave carved this stone.
entries.irish: Nuair a sheasann sé seo chonaic mé uair amháin an drake mór ag eitilt os mo chomhair agus hid mé i mbus go dtí go rith sí. Ulf an Brave snoite an chloch.

entries.english: Let those who read me know not to tarry on these slopes, far from their hearth and the safety of the greenwood. The beasts of the mountains are fell and fierce, hungry for meat, and the worst of these beasts is the cold wind itself. Wear thick furs, build strong fires and keep your bow close at hand.
entries.irish: Lig dóibh siúd a léigh mé a fhios gan tarra ar na fánaí, i bhfad ó a n-croí agus sábháilteacht an greenwood. Na beithigh na sléibhte atá thit agus fíochmhar, ocras le haghaidh feola, agus is é an ceann is measa de na beithigh an ghaoth fuar féin. Caith fionnaidh tiubh, a thógáil dóiteáin láidir agus a choinneáil do Bow gar ar láimh.

entries.english:
Great cities do not rise of themselves

Harden your heart, settler in a strange land

Build from the ground upwards
entries.irish:
Ní cathracha móra ardú féin

Harden do chroí, lonnaitheoir i dtalamh aisteach

Tógáil ón talamh suas

entries.english:
This stone was placed by me, Astrid, in my seventh year in Valheim. At this spot, the Allfather spoke to me. I awoke from a deep sleep to find his words scattered around me on the ground, frozen to pebbles by the deep cold. When I warmed them in my hands they thawed and spoke his message to me, one word after another.

Slay the Forsaken. Chain their heads. I will come.
entries.irish:
Cuireadh an chloch ag dom, Astrid, i mo seachtú bliain i Valheim. Ag an láthair seo, labhair an Allfather liom. Dhúisigh mé ó chodladh domhain chun a chuid focal scaipthe timpeall orm ar an talamh, reoite le púróga ag an fuar domhain. Nuair a warmed mé iad i mo lámha thawed siad agus labhair a teachtaireacht dom, focal amháin i ndiaidh a chéile.

Slay an Forsaken. Slabhra a gceann. Beidh mé ag teacht.

entries.english:
When first I awoke in Valheim, I pleaded with Oden to show himself to me. Where was he? Why had he abandoned me?

For many moons I braved storms and fierce beasts in search of answers. Where were the Gods? Was this to be my reward? Where was Oden?

But now I know. When I pulled up the greydwarfs like weeds from a field or stamped out the surtlings like embers, I did Oden's work. And when I matched my strength against a great wyrm and smote off its head with one blow, I felt Oden's joy within me, deep and proud.

We are Oden's hands, each one of us, and our worth in life is to work his will.
entries.irish:
Nuair a d'éirigh mé ar dtús i Valheim, phléadáil mé le Oden chun é féin a thaispeáint dom. Cá raibh sé? Cén fáth go raibh tréigthe sé dom?

I gcás go leor Gealacha cróga mé stoirmeacha agus beithigh fíochmhar sa tóir ar freagraí. Cá raibh na Dia? An raibh sé seo a bheith ar mo luaíocht? Cá raibh Oden?

Ach anois tá a fhios agam. Nuair a tharraing mé suas an graydwarfs cosúil le fiailí ó réimse nó stampáilte amach na surtlings cosúil le embers, rinne mé obair Oden. Agus nuair a mheaitseáil mé mo neart i gcoinne wyrm mór agus smote as a cheann le buille amháin, Bhraith mé áthas Oden laistigh dom, domhain agus bródúil.

Táimid lámha Oden, gach duine againn, agus is é ár fiú sa saol a bheith ag obair a thoil.

entries.english: Upon this spot, Otho and Bjorn fought a mighty duel to decide who has the finest beard. Now I, Bjorn, must carve this stone to say that the beard of Otho is as bright and beautiful as a corn-field in summer. May almighty Thor tear my own beard from my face if I lie.
entries.irish: Ar an láthair, throid Otho agus Bjorn duel mighty chun cinneadh a bhfuil an féasóg is fearr. Anois, ní mór dom, Bjorn, an chloch seo a fheistiú le rá go bhfuil an féasóg Otho chomh geal agus álainn mar pháirc arbhar sa samhradh. Bealtaine almighty Thor cuimilt mo féasóg féin ó mo aghaidh má luíonn mé.

entries.english:
In Midgard of old, the armies of man pushed back the drakes from the mountains just as the Vanir threw down their mother and cast her into Valheim. But here they have recovered their strength and their numbers. The beat of their mighty wings echoes among the peaks. 

They are fierce and noble creatures, true foes worthy of battle. If they scorn to meet your blade, send your arrows to greet them.
entries.irish:
I Midgard d'aois, an arm an fear bhrú ar ais na drakes ó na sléibhte díreach mar a chaith an Vanir síos a máthair agus chaith sí isteach i Valheim. Ach anseo tá siad a ghnóthú a neart agus a n-uimhreacha. An buille a sciatháin mighty macallaí i measc na beanna.

Tá siad créatúir fíochmhar agus uasal, foes fíor fiú cath. Má scór siad chun freastal ar do lann, a sheoladh do saigheada chun beannú dóibh.

entries.english: In these mountains I cannot throw a spear without hitting something that wants to kill me. But from the heights I have seen sunny plains where life will be easier. I go now to make my home there. These are the words of Ulf.
entries.irish: Sna sléibhte ní féidir liom caith spear gan bualadh rud éigin gur mian a mharú dom. Ach ó na airde tá machairí gréine feicthe agam nuair a bheidh an saol níos éasca. Téim anois a dhéanamh ar mo bhaile ann. Is iad seo na focail de Ulf.

entries.english: There are friends in Valheim but you must seek them amongst your enemies. Old friends, fire-kin, moon-singers. For centuries they have hunted alongside you, now you must remind them of the old covenant between your people and theirs. Flesh is their delight and must be your offering.
entries.irish: Tá cairde i Valheim ach ní mór duit iad a lorg i measc do naimhde. Sean-chairde, tine-craiceann, gealach-singers. Ar feadh na gcéadta bliain tá siad ag fiach taobh leat, anois ní mór duit i gcuimhne dóibh ar an cúnant sean idir do dhaoine agus inniúlacht siúd. Is Flesh a delight agus ní mór a bheith do thairiscint.

entries.english: Ashlands awaits...
entries.irish: Taitneamh a bhaint as Ashlands...

entries.english: Well fought warrior! My brother and I will feast well on this offering! Yet still there is work for your arm… In the Ashlands dark clouds blister the sky and the King stirs on his bed of embers. Until today you have only quarreled. Now you must prepare yourself for war…
entries.irish: Bhuel throid laoch! Mo dheartháir agus beidh mé feast maith ar an tairiscint! Ach fós tá obair do do lámh... Sna scamaill dorcha Ashlands blister an spéir agus an Rí stirs ar a leaba de embers. Go dtí an lá atá inniu ann tá tú quarreled ach amháin. Anois, ní mór duit féin a ullmhú le haghaidh cogaidh...

entries.english: Munin: Introduction
entries.irish: Munin: Réamhrá

entries.english: Kraa! Well met, wanderer… I am Munin, brother to Hugin. I bring greetings from the Allfather. His eye sees through mine, I carry his words beneath my tongue. Keep his ways and I will come to you again…
entries.irish: Kraa! Bhuel bhuail, wanderer... Tá mé Munin, deartháir go Hugin. Tugaim beannachtaí ón Uileathair. Feiceann a shúil trí mhianach, a dhéanamh mé a chuid focal faoi bhun mo theanga. Coinnigh a chuid bealaí agus beidh mé ag teacht chun tú arís...

entries.english:
Where no rain falls

And no crops will grow

Still the ground can give up treasures.
entries.irish:
I gcás nach dtagann aon bháisteach

Agus ní fhásfaidh aon bharra

Fós is féidir leis an talamh a thabhairt suas seoda.

entries.english: This place was too hot for Ulf, a man used to brushing snow from his beard. He carved this stone and moved on.
entries.irish: Bhí an áit seo ró-the do Ulf, fear a úsáidtear chun sneachta a scuabadh óna féasóg. Thóg sé an chloch seo agus bhog sé ar aghaidh.

entries.english: Still your mind, traveller. Oden speaks to those who listen. Here in this barren land, one of the Forsaken Ones dwells. He is an ancient sorcerer twisted by bitterness, dragging what remains of his broken body across the sands. Surely Oden will smile upon the warrior who can vanquish this abhorrence.
entries.irish: Fós d'intinn, taistealaí. Oden Labhraíonn dóibh siúd a éisteacht. Anseo sa talamh barren, ar cheann de na cinn Forsaken dwells. Tá sé ina sorcerer ársa twisted ag bitterness, dragging cad atá fós ar a chorp briste ar fud na gaineamh. Beidh Surely Oden aoibh gháire ar an laoch is féidir a vanquish an abhorrence.

entries.english: In a land far from here I once saw a star come unfastened from the great curtain of night and fall into the sand. It glowed red when I approached but by morning was cool. Blessed sword-flesh, furnace-food, a gift of strong metal from the Gods!
entries.irish: I dtalamh i bhfad ó anseo chonaic mé uair amháin réalta teacht unfastened as an imbhalla mór na hoíche agus titim isteach sa ghaineamh. Glowed sé dearg nuair a chuaigh mé ach ar maidin bhí fionnuar. Blessed sword-flesh, foirnéise-bia, bronntanas de mhiotal láidir ó na Dia!

entries.english:
Good friend, lay your hand on this stone and remember Harald, who carved it. In Midgard I lost my life on the battlefield but in Valheim it was restored to me. Yet still my battles continued.

In the green meadows I fought Eikthyr the Great Stag and lost an eye to his horns.

In the deep woods I gave my shield hand to the Old Man of the Forest, and took a draugr arrow below my ribs that my fingers can still feel.

On the mountainside I fought the Mother Drake and she bit off my leg at the knee so that I must walk always with a staff.

Now my last battle must be at hand. When I sleep this time, where will I wake?
entries.irish:
Dea-chara, leag do lámh ar an gcloch agus cuimhnigh Harald, a snoite é. I Midgard chaill mé mo shaol ar an catha ach i Valheim bhí sé ar ais chugam. Ach fós lean mo cathanna.

Sna móinéir glas throid mé Eikthyr an Stag Mór agus chaill sé súil ar a adharca.

Sna coillte domhain thug mé mo lámh sciath go dtí an Fear Sean na Foraoise, agus thóg arrow draugr thíos mo ribs gur féidir le mo mhéara a bhraitheann go fóill.

Ar an sliabh throid mé an Drake Máthar agus giotán sí amach mo chos ag na glúine ionas nach mór dom siúl i gcónaí le foireann.

Anois ní mór mo cath deiridh a bheith ar láimh. Nuair a chodladh mé an uair seo, áit a dúiseoidh mé?

entries.english: In my dream, Oden came to me as an old man leaning on a stick, a wide-brimmed traveller’s hat on his head. He told me to trust the ravens who carry his words under their tongues and to carve this stone that others might know his will. We must kill the Forsaken to find our places in his hall at Valhalla.
entries.irish: I mo bhrionglóid, tháinig Oden chugam mar shean-fhear ag leanúint ar bata, hata an taistealaí leathan-brimmed ar a cheann. D'inis sé dom muinín a bhaint as na ravens a iompar a chuid focal faoina dteangacha agus a carve an chloch go bhféadfadh daoine eile a fhios a uacht. Ní mór dúinn a mharú an Forsaken chun teacht ar ár n-áiteanna ina halla ag Valhalla.

entries.english: Beneath the ground are the halls of men and women long since gone, ancient tribes who lived in Valheim even before the Allfather turned his eye upon this place. Delve deep to find their treasures but beware, some amongst them do not yet know they are dead.
entries.irish: Tá Beneath an talamh na hallaí na bhfear agus na mban fada ó imithe, treibheanna ársa a bhí ina gcónaí i Valheim fiú sula iompaigh an Allfather a shúil ar an áit seo. Delve domhain a aimsiú a gcuid seoda ach beware, nach bhfuil roinnt ina measc a fhios go fóill go bhfuil siad marbh.

entries.english: From the mountaintop, this plains looked peaceful and pleasant. But I have found it worse than anywhere else. I always hear the buzzing of those thrice-damned insects. My beard has turned as white as snow. I will build a boat.
entries.irish: Ón sliabhraonta, d'fhéach sé seo machairí síochánta agus taitneamhach. Ach fuair mé níos measa ná áit ar bith eile. Cloisim i gcónaí an buzzing de na feithidí thrice-damned. Tá mo féasóg iompaithe mar bán mar sneachta. Tógfaidh mé bád.

entries.english:
What joy it is to roam abroad

With the wind in your hair

And a blue sky before you.


And what joy it is

To stand tall against your foes

And speak plainly to the world.


And then, what joy it is

To come home from your travels

And find the fire still bright in the hearth.
entries.irish:
Cad áthas go bhfuil sé roam thar lear

Leis an ghaoth i do chuid gruaige

Agus spéir gorm roimh tú.


Agus cad áthas é

A seasamh ard i gcoinne do foes

Agus labhairt go soiléir ar fud an domhain.


Agus ansin, cad áthas go bhfuil sé

Chun teacht abhaile ó do taisteal

Agus teacht ar an tine geal fós sa hearth.

entries.english:
On these plains, only the greatest survive to read my words and heed my advice. So heed me now.

Great Oden is not a loving father, kind and gentle, speaking honeyed words. Nor is he a stern liege-lord, arms banded with gold, commanding his thralls on pain of death.

He did not send you here to fight his foes for love or fear of him, but because his foes are your foes. His joy and honour are yours also. You will fight and win just as he once did.

Sons and daughters of Oden, rejoice!
entries.irish:
Ar na machairí, ach an mó maireachtáil a léamh mo focail agus heed mo chomhairle. Mar sin heed mé anois.

Ní mór Oden athair grámhara, cineál agus milis, labhairt focail miled. Ná tá sé ina luí Stern-lord, arm banded le hór, i gceannas ar a thralls ar pian an bháis.

Ní raibh sé a sheolann tú anseo chun troid a foes le haghaidh grá nó eagla air, ach toisc go bhfuil a foes do foes. Tá a áthas agus onóir mise freisin. Beidh tú ag troid agus bua díreach mar a rinne sé uair amháin.

Mac agus iníonacha Oden, rejoice!

entries.english:
Here on the plains you will find the dwellings of the Fuling, that ancient race who once built towers and cities to rival those of men until Oden punished them for their pride. He trampled the Fuling armies, their armour cracking like snail shells beneath his feet, and tore down their cities.

Only Yagluth, the great sorcerer, would not bend or break before his fury. So Oden tore his body in half and cast the remains into Valheim, where he bled into the earth and crumbled to dust, wept over by the last of his people.

Now the Fuling rule over the plains of Valheim, savage and wild with only hatred and fear in their hearts. But Yagluth is with them still, an unseen force that the Fuling shamans draw upon for their crooked magic, growing again in strength as his people spread across the world...
entries.irish:
Anseo ar na machairí gheobhaidh tú na teaghaisí an Fuling, go cine ársa a thóg uair túir agus cathracha a rival siúd na bhfear go dtí Oden phionósú dóibh as a n-bród. trampled sé an arm Fuling, a n-arm scáineadh cosúil le sliogáin seil faoi bhun a chosa, agus Strac síos a gcathracha.

Ní bheadh ach Yagluth, an sorcerer mór, Bend nó briseadh roimh a Fury. Mar sin, tore Oden a chorp i leath agus chaith na hiarsmaí isteach i Valheim, áit a bled sé isteach sa talamh agus crumbled go deannaigh, wept thar ag an ceann deireanach de chuid daoine.

Anois an riail Fuling thar na machairí de Valheim, savage agus fiáin le fuath amháin agus eagla ina gcroí. Ach tá Yagluth leo fós, fórsa gan choinne a tharraingt ar an shamans Fuling as a n-draíocht cam, ag fás arís i neart mar a scaipeadh a chuid daoine ar fud an domhain...

entries.english: The lox are mighty creatures, great earth-shakers who roamed the plains of Valheim long before the Forsaken were banished to this realm. They are quick to anger and will crush any who are foolish enough to approach them unguarded, but they have known the hand of man and can be taught to love it again.
entries.irish: Is iad na lox créatúir mighty, mór-shakers talún a roamed an machairí de Valheim fada sular cuireadh an Forsaken banished leis an réimse seo. Tá siad tapa a fearg agus beidh crush aon atá foolish go leor chun cur chuige iad unguarded, ach tá siad ar eolas ar an láimh an duine agus is féidir a mhúineadh chun grá é arís.

entries.english: Know, traveler, that while you cannot die in the world of Valheim, yet you can cease to be reborn. Many are those who have come before you to work the will of Oden, only to find their own will failing...
entries.irish: Know, lucht siúil, go cé nach féidir leat bás i saol na Valheim, ach is féidir leat a bheith reborn. Tá go leor acu siúd a tháinig roimh tú a bheith ag obair ar an toil Oden, ach amháin chun teacht ar a gcuid féin ag teip...

entries.english: We sealed the door and scattered the key. Leave her be.
entries.irish: séalaithe muid an doras agus scaipthe ar an eochair. Fág di a bheith.

entries.english:
Let you who read me know of the Surtlings, that you might not fall prey to their wickedness.

Long ago the great demon Surtr was brought down and destroyed by the First Men, giant warriors of whom you are but a dwindling echo. They smote long upon the body of this Surtr with swords and hammers so that his fiery substance was shattered into many small pieces.

He who was made of the fire was fire in every part of him. You could not say ‘Here is the brain of Surtr’ or ‘Here is Surtr’s liver’ because every part was Surtr. So all the fragments of him were Surtr still, only much weaker in power and in thought and in memory, with no way to become whole once again.

Now we call these fragments Surtlings and when they are found they should be stamped out like the last embers of a fire or doused with water to choke off their flames at the root. They will throw fire from afar and joy in causing terror and destruction. Even in his scattered dotage, the demon seeks revenge on the children of the First Men.
entries.irish:
Lig duit a léamh a fhios agam de na Surtlings, nach bhféadfadh tú titim chreiche a n wickedness.

Fada ó shin tugadh an Surtr Demon mór síos agus scriosta ag an Chéad Fir, laochra ollmhór a bhfuil tú ach macalla dwindling. smote siad fada ar an comhlacht seo Surtr le claimhte agus casúir ionas go raibh a substaint fiery shattered i go leor píosaí beaga.

Bhí sé a bhí déanta as an tine tine i ngach cuid de dó. Ní fhéadfaí tú a rá 'Anseo é an inchinn Surtr' nó 'Anseo é ae Surtr' toisc go raibh gach cuid Surtr. Mar sin, bhí na blúirí de dó fós Surtr, ach i bhfad níos laige i gcumhacht agus i smaoinimh agus i gcuimhne, gan aon bhealach a bheith ina n-iomláine arís.

Anois, glaoimid ar na blúirí Surtlings agus nuair a bhíonn siad le fáil ba chóir iad a stampáil amach mar na embers deiridh de tine nó doused le huisce a lasracha ag an fhréamh. Beidh siad caith tine ó afar agus áthas i cúis terror agus scrios. Fiú amháin ina dotage scaipthe, lorgaíonn an Demon díoltas ar na páistí an Chéad Fir.

entries.english: Lore: Surtlings
entries.irish: cliceáil grianghraf a mhéadú

entries.english: Heed the words of poor Ulf and do not build your house beside the murky waters. Bad dreams and a soggy bed are all you will find. I leave this stone as a warning and go now to make my dwelling on higher ground.
entries.irish: Heed na focail de Ulf bocht agus nach thógáil do theach in aice leis na huiscí murky. Tá aisling folctha agus leaba soggy go léir a gheobhaidh tú. Fágann mé an chloch seo mar rabhadh agus téigh anois chun mo theaghais a dhéanamh ar an talamh níos airde.

entries.english: Linger not, traveller. The air is pestilent and the water poison. The Draugr walk here and the thing I will not name stirs below the surface, a bitter mass of bone and sin. Tread carefully and quickly until you feel the sun on your face once more.
entries.irish: Gan an lucht siúil. Tá an t-aer pestilent agus an nimh uisce. Siúlóid an Draugr anseo agus an rud nach mbeidh mé ainm stirs faoi bhun an dromchla, mais searbh de chnámh agus pheaca. Arán go cúramach agus go tapa go dtí go mbraitheann tú an ghrian ar do aghaidh uair amháin níos mó.

entries.english: In this gloomy region you may yet find something which shines. War-flesh, warrior's gold, bread of the forge... Bright iron is here for those who will take it!
entries.irish: Sa réigiún seo gloomy is féidir leat teacht ar rud éigin a shines. Cogadh-flesh, óir laochra, arán an forge... Tá iarann geal anseo dóibh siúd a thógfaidh é!

entries.english: You who pass, remember me. I am a man whose home was once in the mountains of Midgard, carried here when I thought to earn my rest, to find a life after life in Valheim. There were seven of us before the Greydwarfs came. Now Oden will not hear me and the seas refuse me. Soon this stone will be all that remains.
entries.irish: Tá tú a pas, cuimhnigh dom. Tá mé fear a bhfuil a bhaile a bhí uair amháin i sléibhte Midgard, rinneadh anseo nuair a shíl mé a thuilleamh mo chuid eile, a fháil ar an saol tar éis an tsaoil i Valheim. Bhí seacht againn sular tháinig an Greydwarfs. Anois ní éistfidh Oden dom agus diúltóidh na farraigí dom. Go gairid beidh an chloch seo go léir atá fós.

entries.english: Beware the surtlings, embers of a great fire long ago stamped to ashes. They are drawn to the swamp in numbers but their lights can be seen from afar. Keep to the high ground.
entries.irish: Beware na surtlings, embers de tine mór i bhfad ó shin stampáilte le luaithreach. Déantar iad a tharraingt chuig an swamp in uimhreacha ach is féidir a gcuid soilse a fheiceáil ó i bhfad. Coinnigh ar an talamh ard.

entries.english: In centuries past, the Draugr walked these lands just as you do now. Pity them, caught between the living and the dead in a shadow of the world they once knew. To destroy them is a mercy.
entries.irish: Sna céadta bliain anuas, shiúil an Draugr na tailte díreach mar a dhéanann tú anois. Pity iad, gafa idir an maireachtála agus na marbh i scáth an domhain a fhios acu uair amháin. Chun iad a scrios trócaire.

entries.english:
Below the mist and murk

Bone speaks to bone

Remembering flesh.
entries.irish:
Thíos an mist agus murk

Labhraíonn duine le cnámh

Ag cuimhneamh flesh.

entries.english:
For long ages, Oden's eye was turned from Valheim. Yet while the Gods ignored it, other creatures crept or fell through cracks into the forgotten world. Trolls, goblins and men found their way along these secret paths. Kingdoms rose and fell, and are buried deep beneath the ground.

Walker among the dead, you tread a grave with every step.
entries.irish:
Le haghaidh aoiseanna fada, bhí iompú súil Oden ó Valheim. Ach cé neamhaird na Dia é, créatúir eile crept nó thit trí scoilteanna ar fud an domhain dearmad. Trolls, goblins agus fir a fuair a mbealach feadh na cosáin rúnda. D'ardaigh agus thit Ríocht, agus tá siad curtha domhain faoi bhun na talún.

Walker i measc na marbh, tú tread uaigh le gach céim.

entries.english: At this place I killed seven of the draugr and ended their long years of fighting and misery. Now who will end mine?
entries.irish: Ag an áit seo mharaigh mé seacht den draugr agus chríochnaigh a gcuid blianta fada de troid agus misery. Anois a chuirfidh deireadh le mianach?

entries.english: I am Gudrun, no man's wife, no father's daughter. Only my name remains to me. But sometimes when I wake I feel the weight of a babe at my breast and I cry. Great Freya take pity on me.
entries.irish: Tá mé Gudrun, aon fear bean chéile, aon athair iníon. Níl ach mo ainm fós dom. Ach uaireanta nuair a dúisigh mé bhraitheann mé an meáchan de babe ag mo chíche agus mé caoin. Great Freya ghlacadh trua ar dom.

entries.english: Fear not that the Gods have abandoned you. Valheim drifts from the world tree and the Vanir cannot come in arms to this world but still they watch from afar. Keep them ever in your mind. If your faith is strong, they may send you a sign.
entries.irish: Fear nach bhfuil go bhfuil na Dia tréigthe agat. Ní féidir le Valheim sruthanna ón gcrann domhanda agus ón Vanir teacht in airm go dtí an domhan seo ach fós iad ag breathnú ó i bhfad. Coinnigh iad riamh i d'intinn. Má tá do chreideamh láidir, d'fhéadfadh siad a sheoladh tú comhartha.

entries.english:
There is no death that does not bring new life. As worms feed on the battlefield, so did the great corpses of Oden's enemies bring new life to Valheim. Lesser creatures fed on their flesh, fattening themselves on the ancient magic that still clung to them. Their spirits trickled into the earth to renew the soil, or sought out new bodies for themselves.

Do not scorn the dead, you who are dead yourself.
entries.irish:
Níl aon bhás nach bhfuil a thabhairt saol nua. Mar worms beatha ar an catha, mar sin rinne an corpses mór naimhde Oden a thabhairt saol nua a Valheim. créatúir níos lú chothaithe ar a flesh, ramhrú iad féin ar an draíocht ársa go fós clung leo. A gcuid biotáillí trickled isteach sa domhan a athnuachan an ithir, nó lorg comhlachtaí nua dóibh féin.

Ná scor na marbh, tú atá marbh féin.

entries.english: Ingrid and Torgunn decided to honour the gods in this place. They smiled upon Ingrid, granting her a great boon. Torgunn on the other hand, was made all too aware of the risk she was taking, as her blade shattered into pieces upon the altar. She raised this stone to warn others of the risk attempting refinement at this forge!
entries.irish: Chinn Ingrid agus Torgunn ómós a thabhairt do na déithe san áit seo. Shíl siad ar Ingrid, a dheonú di boon mór. Torgunn ar an láimh eile, rinneadh go léir ró-eolach ar an riosca a bhí sí ag cur, mar a lann shattered i bpíosaí ar an altóir. D'ardaigh sí an chloch seo chun rabhadh a thabhairt do dhaoine eile den bheachtú riosca atá ag iarraidh a dhéanamh ar an mbás seo!

entries.english: Lore: Forge of Potential
entries.irish: Iasacht: Toradh féideartha

entries.english:
The glowing creatures are an excellent source of light in the dark.
Perhaps a wooden cage might serve to keep them in place.
entries.irish:
Tá na créatúir glowing foinse den scoth de solas sa dorchadas.
B'fhéidir go bhféadfadh Cage adhmaid freastal orthu a choinneáil i bhfeidhm.

entries.english:
Rest, wanderer, and consider the wraiths.

We know that when a warrior dies, their soul cracks open and seeps into the earth around them, thereby to nourish new life and strengthen those who follow after.

Yet if a warrior should die with no great deeds to their name, their soul will be too thin and airy. It will flow upwards instead, like smoke from a hearth. These wisps of souls sometimes catch in the branches of trees long enough to form wraiths, wretched shadows with nothing but bitterness and jealousy to drive them. Blown about the land in despair, they remain only to prey on those who are still living.

Should you see one, kill it and count it a mercy.
entries.irish:
Rest, wanderer, agus a mheas na wraiths.

Tá a fhios againn go nuair a fhaigheann laoch bás, a scoilteanna anam oscailte agus seeps isteach sa domhan timpeall orthu, rud a nourish saol nua agus iad siúd a leanann tar éis a neartú.

Ach más rud é gur chóir laochra bás gan aon gníomhais mór a n-ainm, beidh a n-anam a bheith ró-tanaí agus airy. Beidh sé sreabhadh suas ina ionad sin, cosúil le deataigh ó hearth. Na wisps anamacha ghabháil uaireanta i na brainsí na gcrann fada go leor chun foirm wraiths, scáthanna wretched le rud ar bith ach bitterness agus éad chun iad a thiomáint. Blown mar gheall ar an talamh i éadóchas, tá siad fós ach a chreiche ar iad siúd atá fós ina gcónaí.

Ba chóir duit a fheiceáil amháin, é a mharú agus é a chomhaireamh trócaire.

entries.english: Lore: Wraiths
entries.irish: Naisc go dtí suíomhanna eile
